question: In CIViC, what is the clinical implication of ERBB2 Amplification for Neratinib, Trastuzumab in Her2-receptor Positive Breast Cancer?
evidence_text: In this two arm, Phase III study (NCT00878709) of the efficacy of a 12 month course of the TKI neratinib after trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy of early stage HER2-positive breast cancer was assessed using invasive disease-free survival as primary endpoint. HER2 positivity was assessed via FISH. At 2 year follow-up, 70 vs. 109 disease-free survival events had occurred and disease-free survival rates were 93.9% vs. 91.6% (significant) in neratinib vs. placebo groups respectively. Distant disease-free survival and time to distant recurrence were similar in both groups. These results are an interesting contrast to results of long-term adjuvant therapy with trastuzumab (HERA) which did not show significant benefit.

question: In CIViC, what is the clinical implication of ERBB2 Amplification for Trastuzumab in Her2-receptor Positive Breast Cancer?
evidence_text: HERA was a Phase III trial assessing application of trastuzumab in an extended adjuvant setting. Patients were HER2 positive with completely excised invasive BC, node positive or negative, and having undergone prior adjuvant or neo-adjuvant chemotherapy. In the 3 arm study patients were given trastuzumab courses of 1 year, 2 years, or untreated. At the first planned interim analysis, trastuzumab treatment for one year was compared with observation alone. A significant difference in disease-free survival was seen with 220 DFS events out of 1693 in the observation arm versus 127 DFS events out of 1694 in the 1 year trastuzumab arm. 1 year adjuvant trastuzumab is currently the standard of care.

question: In CIViC, what is the clinical implication of ERBB2 Amplification for Margetuximab in Breast Cancer?
evidence_text: In this phase III, randomized, open-label trial, 536 patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who have received two or more prior anti-HER2 regimens, with at least one being for metastatic disease. The patients were randomized 1:1 to margetuximab 15 mg/kg or trastuzumab 6 mg/kg (loading dose of 8 mg/kg), each in 3-week cycles. The primary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). The study found that margetuximab improved primary PFS over trastuzumab (HR, 0.76; 95% CI: 0.59 - 0.98; p = .03; median, 5.8 [95% CI: 5.5 - 7.0] months versus 4.9 [95% CI: 4.2 - 5.6] months). At the second interim analysis of 270 deaths, the median OS was 21.6 months for margetuximab versus 19.8 months with trastuzumab (HR, 0.89; 95% CI: 0.69 - 1.13; p = .33, and PFS showed relative risk reduction favouring margetuximab (HR, 0.71; 95% CI: 0.58 - 0.86; p < .001; median, 5.7 versus 4.4 months). Margetuximab improved ORR over trastuzumab at both times of analysis on October 10th, 2018, and September 10th, 2019: 22% vs 16% (p = .06;) and 25% vs 14% (p < .001) respectively.

evidence_text: In this open-label, randomized, phase II trial, 187 patients with HER2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma that had progressed while they were receiving at least two previous therapies, including trastuzumab, were randomized in a 2:1 to receive trastuzumab deruxtecan (6.4 mg/kg body weight every 3 weeks) or the physician’s choice of chemotherapy (55 received irinotecan and 7 paclitaxel). 51% of patients in the trastuzumab deruxtecan cohort had an objective response, compared to 14% in the chemotherapy cohort (p < 0.001). Overall survival was longer with trastuzumab deruxtecan cohort compared to the chemotherapy cohort (median, 12.5 versus 8.4 months; HR, 0.59; 95% CI: 0.39 - 0.88; p = 0.01). The median progression-free survival was 5.6 months (95% CI: 4.3 - 6.9) in the trastuzumab deruxtecan cohort versus 3.5 months (95% CI: 2.0 - 4.3) in the chemotherapy cohort (HR, 0.47; 95% CI: 0.31 - 0.71).

question: In CIViC, what is the clinical implication of KRAS Wildtype for Cetuximab, Chemotherapy in Colorectal Cancer?
evidence_text: In this open-label, randomized, controlled, phase III trial, 1,198 patients with histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum and immunohistochemical evidence of tumour EGFR expression were randomized 1:1 to receive cetuximab plus FOLFIRI and FOLFIRI alone. The FOLFIRI regimen was dosed as follows: 30- to 90-minute infusion of irinotecan at a dose of 180 mg per square meter of body-surface area; an infusion, for 120 minutes, of racemic leucovorin or L-leucovorin at a dose of 400 or 200 mg, respectively, per square meter of body-surface area; fluorouracil in a bolus of 400 mg per square meter of body-surface area and then continuous infusion for 46 hours of 2400 mg per square meter of body-surface area. Cetuximab was dosed at an initial 120-minute infusion on day 1 of 400 mg per square meter of body-surface area, followed by 60-minute infusions of cetuximab at a dose of 250 mg per square meter of body-surface area, once weekly. The hazard ratio for progression-free survival in the cetuximab cohort compared to the FOLFIRI cohort was 0.85 (95% CI: 0.72 - 0.99; p = 0.048). Further, the two treatment regimens had no significant difference in overall survival (HR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.81 - 1.07; p = 0.31). There was a significant interaction between the treatment group and KRAS mutation status for tumour response (p = 0.03) but not for progression-free survival (PFS) (p = 0.07) or overall survival (p = 0.44). Lastly, the hazard ratio for PFS among patients with wild-type KRAS tumours was 0.68 (95% CI: 0.50 - 0.94), in favour of the cetuximab cohort.

question: In CIViC, what is the clinical implication of KRAS Wildtype for Panitumumab, Chemotherapy in Colorectal Cancer?
evidence_text: In this randomized, phase III trial, 1,183 patients with previously untreated metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum, were randomized 1:1 to receive panitumumab-FOLFOX4 versus FOLFOX4. Panitumumab was administered IV over 1 hour at 6 mg/kg every 2 weeks on day 1 before FOLFOX4 chemotherapy. If tolerated, later infusions could be administered over 30 minutes. FOLFOX4 was administered every 2 weeks and dosed as follows: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 IV infusion on day 1 and leucovorin 200 mg/m2 (or equivalent) IV infusion followed by fluorouracil 400 mg/m2 IV bolus and 600 mg/m2 22-hour continuous infusion on days 1 and 2. For patients with a wild-type KRAS, panitumumab-FOLFOX4 significantly improved progression-free survival compared with FOLFOX4 alone (median PFS of 9.6 versus 8.0 months, respectively; HR, 0.80; 95% CI: 0.66 - 0.97; p = .02). In terms of overall survival, a nonsignificant increase was observed for panitumumab-FOLFOX4 versus FOLFOX4 (median OS, 23.9 versus 19.7 months, respectively; HR, 0.83; 95% CI: 0.67 - 1.02; p = .072). For patients with mutant KRAS PFS was significantly reduced in the panitumumab-FOLFOX4 cohort versus the FOLFOX4 cohort (HR, 1.29; 95% CI: 1.04 - 1.62; p = .02), and median overall survival was 15.5 months versus 19.3 months, respectively (HR, 1.24; 95% CI: 0.98 - 1.57; p = .068).

question: In CIViC, what is the clinical implication of EGFR Amplification OR EGFR Alteration for Lenvatinib in Hepatocellular Carcinoma?
evidence_text: The ctDNA of 46 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma was analyzed to investigate whether EGFR alterations could lead to lenvatinib resistance. Among these patients, 16 had been treated with lenvatinib, and 30 had received immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). At the time of disease progression, EGFR amplification was observed in one patient who had normal baseline EGFR levels, and in another patient, EGFR amplification increased from 4.8 to 7 copies. To retrospectively assess whether lenvatinib treatment suggested early treatment failure, three patient cohorts were established: those with EGFR/ERBB2 alterations before lenvatinib treatment (cohort 1; n = 6), those without EGFR/ERBB2 alterations prior to treatment (cohort 2; n = 32), and those with EGFR/ERBB2 alterations before ICI treatment (cohort 3; n = 17). The median PFS in cohort 1 was lower (2.2 months; 95% CI: 1.6-2.8) than in cohort 2 (5.9 months; 95% CI: 2.0-9.8) and cohort 3 (7.1 months; 95% CI: 1.0-13.2). Similarly, the median OS was also shorter in cohort 1 (3.9 months; 95% CI: 0.5-7.3) compared to cohort 2 (9.2 months; 95% CI: 7.3-11.1) and cohort 3 (16.9 months; 95% CI: 6.2-27.6). These findings suggest that EGFR alterations may be a key mechanism driving lenvatinib resistance.

question: In CIViC, what is the clinical implication of BRAF V600E for Encorafenib, Cetuximab in Colorectal Cancer?

Patients with bTMB ≥ 16 achieved superior survival over chemotherapy for both durvalumab (OS HR: 0.39; PFS HR: 0.48) and combination therapy (OS HR: 0.38; PFS HR: 0.45).
